NOTES
  NOTE "Client: 41yo male, intermediate, recently ill with 3 weeks off, ~4kg weight loss. Pre-illness strength: bench 100kg, squat 140kg, deadlift 170kg."
  NOTE "Primary goal: regain lost body mass and support recovery and training during the 3-week reconditioning block."
  NOTE "Recommended approach: modest calorie surplus with emphasis on protein, adequate carbs around training, and sufficient fats and micronutrients."
  NOTE "Estimate maintenance calories (pre-illness activity): ~15 kcal/kg/day. For a 80kg client (example): maintenance ~1200 kcal/day — adjust using actual bodyweight. (If client provides exact bodyweight, recalc.)"
  NOTE "Target calorie intake:"
  NOTE "- Short-term target: +250 kcal/day above current estimated maintenance for 3 weeks to regain ~0.5kg per week conservatively."
  NOTE "- If client is significantly fatigued or appetite limited, start with maintenance +100..150 kcal/day and increase as tolerated."
  NOTE "Protein:"
  NOTE "- 1.6..2.2 g/kg/day. Prefer 2.0 g/kg/day while refeeding to support lean mass recovery. Example: 80kg -> 160 g protein/day."
  NOTE "Carbohydrate:"
  NOTE "- 3..5 g/kg/day on average; increase to 4..6 g/kg on heavy training days or long run days to support glycogen repletion. Example: 80kg -> 320 g carbs on heavier days (~4 g/kg)."
  NOTE "Fat:"
  NOTE "- Fill remaining calories with fats (~20..30% of total calories). Aim for 0.8..1.2 g/kg/day. Example: 80kg -> 64..96 g fat/day."
  NOTE "Meal timing and peri-workout:"
  NOTE "- Consume 0.4..0.6 g/kg carbohydrate and 20..30 g protein in the 1..2h before training if tolerated."
  NOTE "- Within 1h post-training aim for 0.4..0.6 g/kg carbohydrate + 20..40 g protein to assist recovery."
  NOTE "Hydration & micronutrients:"
  NOTE "- Prioritize fluid, electrolyte replacement if fevered. Include varied vegetables, fruit, and whole grains; consider a multivitamin if intake is restricted."
  NOTE "Progress monitoring:"
  NOTE "- Track weight 2x/week, aim to regain ~0.25..0.5 kg/week. If no weight gain in 7–10 days, increase daily intake by ~200–300 kcal."
  NOTE "- Monitor fatigue, sleep, resting heart rate. If persistent high fatigue, reduce training load and prioritize additional calories and sleep."
  NOTE "Other practical tips:"
  NOTE "- Prefer energy-dense, nutrient-rich foods if appetite low: smoothies with milk/yogurt, nut butters, oats, avocado, olive oil, whole-fat dairy."
  NOTE "- Spread protein across 3–5 meals, include a protein-rich snack before bed (e.g., cottage cheese, Greek yogurt) if appropriate."
  NOTE "Safety:"
  NOTE "- If any new symptoms emerge (prolonged tachycardia, chest pain, breathlessness), stop intensified training and seek medical review."
PHASES_END

PLAN "Assessment: Jumping to Pre-Illness Loads"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary:
    name "Assess safety of returning to pre-illness loads"

PHASES
  PHASE "Decision Guidance" (1 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 0m "Assessment Checklist":
        warmup:
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x1..1 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1m
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Tuesday training 0m "Considerations":
        warmup:
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x1..1 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1m
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Wednesday training 0m "Risk Mitigation Steps":
        warmup:
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x1..1 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1m

NOTES
  NOTE "Context: client 41M, returned from 3 weeks off with mild flu, 4kg weight loss, pre-illness estimated 1RMs bench 100kg, squat 140kg, deadlift 170kg."
  NOTE "Short answer: jumping immediately to pre-illness 1RM loads carries increased risk. Even with 'normal' energy today, recent illness, weight loss, and deconditioning can reduce resilience, increase fatigue, and impair technique and recovery."
  NOTE "Physiological reasons to be cautious:"
  NOTE "- Reduced glycogen and lean mass after illness and weight loss can make heavy lifts feel harder and raise injury risk."
  NOTE "- Immune system recovery and residual inflammation may persist beyond symptom resolution."
  NOTE "- Cardiovascular strain and autonomic alterations can occur post-viral; sudden high CNS load (near-max lifts) may provoke excessive fatigue."
  NOTE "Practical guideline (recommended):"
  NOTE "- Avoid testing true 1RM or consistently training at pre-illness 1RM for at least 7–14 days post-illness even if energy feels normal."
  NOTE "- If client insists on heavier work, use graded approach: start with ~80..85% of pre-illness 1RM for 1–2 sessions with conservative volume and monitor response."
  NOTE "Example conservative starting loads (single-session testing progression):"
  NOTE "- Bench: start session working sets at ~80% of 100kg = 80kg (e.g., 3x3..5 rpe 7). If all sets feel RPE ≤7 and recovery is good next 48h, progress next upper session toward 90%."
  NOTE "-Squat: start at ~80% of 140kg = 112kg (e.g., 3x3..5 rpe 7). Progress cautiously if well recovered."
  NOTE "-Deadlift: start at ~80% of 170kg = 136kg (e.g., 3x2..3 rpe 7). Use lower volume and longer rests."
  NOTE "Monitoring and criteria to advance to pre-illness loads:"
  NOTE "- Objective: perform prescribed session with target RPE or lower, maintain movement quality, and have minimal undue fatigue in 24–72h (sleep, appetite, mood, HR, soreness)."
  NOTE "- If resting heart rate elevated >5–10 bpm, sleep worsened, or excessive soreness/fatigue occurs, reduce loads/volume and re-evaluate."
  NOTE "If client still prefers direct plan to start heavier, recommended protocol (example 2-week ramp):"
  NOTE "- Week A (first 3–7 days): work at 75..85% of pre-illness 1RM on main lifts, reduced volume (~60–75% normal sets), RPE target 6..7."
  NOTE "- Week B (after favourable response): increase to 85..92% for low-rep sets, gradually restore volume; consider testing single heavy rep only if recovery markers are normal."
  NOTE "Safety alternatives to max testing:"
  NOTE "- Use RPE and bar speed as real-time gauges — stop if RPE drifts above target or bar speed slows markedly."
  NOTE "- Prioritize technique warm-up sets and include extra warm-up sets before heavy attempts."
  NOTE "- Maintain enhanced nutrition (calorie/protein), sleep, and reduce other stressors during reconditioning."
  NOTE "Final recommendation:"
  NOTE "- Do not immediately return to full pre-illness 1RM loads across the board. A measured ramp (start ~80% with conservative volume) is the safest and most reliable way to return to baseline while minimising injury and setbacks."
PHASES_END

PLAN "Readiness Criteria for Full Intensity Return"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL readiness:
    name "Objective signals to resume full intensity training"

PHASES
  PHASE "Readiness Signals" (1 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 0m "Baseline Metrics":
        warmup:
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x1..1 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1m
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Tuesday training 0m "Performance Signals":
        warmup:
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x1..1 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1m
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Wednesday training 0m "Recovery Signals":
        warmup:
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x1..1 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1m

NOTES
  NOTE "Use a combination of objective measures, performance markers, and subjective reporting. Require multiple favourable signals across 48–72h before returning to full intensity."
  NOTE "1) Resting metrics (objective):"
  NOTE "- Resting heart rate: returned to within ~5 bpm of pre-illness baseline for 2 consecutive mornings."
  NOTE "- Sleep quality: similar duration and restorative feeling to pre-illness for 2 nights."
  NOTE "- Appetite & weight: appetite normal; weight trending toward baseline or stable (no further unintended loss) over 7 days."
  NOTE "2) Symptom/health status (absolute requirements):"
  NOTE "- Fully resolved symptoms (no fever, no chest pain, no significant breathlessness, no dizziness)."
  NOTE "- No new cardiac or respiratory symptoms with low-level exertion (walking, easy run). If present, seek medical evaluation before heavy lifting."
  NOTE "3) Performance markers in training (functional readiness):"
  NOTE "- Able to complete two consecutive training sessions (48–72h apart) at prescribed submaximal loads (≈75–85% pre-illness 1RM) with target RPE (≤7) and preserved technique."
  NOTE "- Bar speed / movement quality: minimal velocity loss across sets; technique remains consistent without compensations."
  NOTE "- Repeated-set performance: minimal drop in reps achieved at target RPE across sets (≤1 rep loss across sets at given load)."
  NOTE "4) Recovery response (24–72h after sessions):"
  NOTE "- Muscle soreness is within expected range and not progressive; energy and mood are maintained or improved."
  NOTE "- No marked increase in resting heart rate (>5–10 bpm), no prolonged excessive fatigue, and sleep not more disturbed."
  NOTE "5) Autonomic and subjective readiness:"
  NOTE "- Subjective energy and motivation consistent across the day; perceived exertion aligns with expected RPE for sessions."
  NOTE "- No orthostatic symptoms (lightheadedness on standing)."
  NOTE "6) Nutrition & hydration supportive:"
  NOTE "- Calorie and protein targets being met to support higher intensity (see nutrition plan). Hydration adequate."
  NOTE "7) Practical progression rules to full intensity:"
  NOTE "- Step 1: Complete 2 sessions at ~75–85% 1RM (RPE ≤7) with normal recovery."
  NOTE "- Step 2: Increase to 85–92% 1RM for low-volume sets (singles/doubles or 3x2) for 1–2 sessions; monitor recovery."
  NOTE "- Step 3: If all markers remain favourable, reintroduce normal volume at target intensities over 1–2 weeks; avoid testing new 1RM earlier than ~14 days post-illness unless all signals are strongly positive."
  NOTE "8) Red flags (stop and reassess / seek medical advice):"
  NOTE "- Chest pain, palpitations with exercise, undue breathlessness, syncope, marked and persistent tachycardia, or collapse of performance with poor recovery."
  NOTE "- Persistent or worsening fatigue despite rest and nutrition, or weight loss continues."
  NOTE "9) Logging and decision-making:"
  NOTE "- Track: morning RHR, sleep quality, bodyweight (2x/week), session RPE, set performance, and subjective energy."
  NOTE "- If 5+ of the favourable signals above are met consistently over 7 days, progressing to full intensity is reasonable. If fewer, continue graded return and reassess."
PHASES_END
